item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 030529
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Wed Sep 2 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Karina, located well east of the Hawaiian Islands, on Hurricane
Lowell, located several hundred miles south of the Hawaiian Islands,
and on recently upgraded Hurricane Marie, located several hundred
miles southwest of the southern tip of the Baja California
Peninsula.

Offshore of Southwestern Mexico:
An area of low pressure could form well offshore of southwestern
Mexico over the weekend or early next week. Gradual development is
possible, and the system could become a tropical depression
around the middle of next week while it moves west-northwestward
at 10 to 15 mph, likely remaining well offshore of Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...40 percent.

$$
Forecaster Pasch

DAYS...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1100 PM HST...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...19.6N 135.7W
ABOUT 1260 MI...2030 KM E OF HILO HAWAII
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...120 MPH...195 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 285 DEGREES AT 12 MPH...19 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...957 MB...28.26 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 PM HST (0900 UTC), the center of Hurricane Karina was
located near latitude 19.6 North, longitude 135.7 West.  Karina is
moving toward the west-northwest near 12 mph (19 km/h), and this
general motion is expected to continue for the next couple of days, 
with a more northwestward motion by this weekend.
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to near 120 mph (195 km/h) 
with higher gusts.  Karina is a category 3 hurricane on the 
Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale.  Gradual weakening is forecast 
during the next several days.  However, Karina is expected to 
remain a hurricane for the next couple of days.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 35 miles (55 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 125 miles
(205 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 957 mb (28.26 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 500 AM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Pasch

item.title: Hurricane Karina Forecast Discussion Number 27
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM HST Wed Sep 02 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 030239
TCDEP1
 
Hurricane Karina Discussion Number  27
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP112026
500 PM HST Wed Sep 02 2026

Latest infrared satellite imagery of Karina suggests that convective 
cloud-top temperatures continue to warm. Karina continues to 
maintain an annular appearance, while the eye remains cloud-filled. 
The latest TAFB subjective Dvorak intensity estimate held steady 
from 18z to 00z, at 5.5/6.5 or 127 kt. Objective intensity estimates 
from CIMSS vary around 105-110 kt. Given the warming cloud-top 
temperatures over the last several hours, the initial intensity 
estimate was adjusted down slightly to 115 kt. 

Karina is currently moving west-northwestward around 9 kt. A 
subtropical ridge to the north of Karina should cause the cyclone to 
continue moving west-northwestward for the next couple of days.  
Karina is then expected to turn more northwesterly later this week 
as the subtropical ridge is weakened by an oncoming upper-level 
trough.  Karina's track forecast was nudged slightly to the east of 
the previous forecast, reflecting a blend of HCCA and GDMI. Models 
exhibit relatively strong agreement in Karina's track through the 
first 48 h, before spread increases thereafter.

While vertical wind shear is expected to remain very weak over the 
next 48 h, Karina is expected to track toward cooler SSTs and into 
a drier mid-level environment. The latest NHC intensity forecast 
shows a slightly faster rate of weakening than the previous 
forecast, but still lies at the high end of the guidance envelope 
for the first 3 days, and then closer to the intensity consensus 
at days 4 and 5. The hostile environmental conditions should 
cause Karina to lose its convection and become post-tropical by 
day 5.

----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...18.9N 113.9W
ABOUT 380 MI...610 KM SW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA

PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 300 DEGREES AT 10 MPH...17 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...981 MB...28.97 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 AM MST (0900 UTC), the center of Hurricane Marie was located
near latitude 18.9 North, longitude 113.9 West. Marie is moving
toward the west-northwest near 10 mph (17 km/h), and this motion 
should continue for the next few days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 85 mph (140 km/h) with higher
gusts.  Some strengthening is forecast during the next 48 hours, 
and gradual weakening is anticipated to begin by this weekend.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 40 miles (65 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 205 miles
(335 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 981 mb (28.97 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Marie will affect portions of the coast of
southwest Mexico and the Baja California Peninsula for the next few
days and will likely spread northward to southern California over
the weekend.  These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf
and rip current conditions. Please consult products from your local
weather office. A depiction of rip current risk for the United
States can be found at:
hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep1.shtml?ripCurrents
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 AM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Blake

item.title: Hurricane Marie Forecast Discussion Number 9
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM MST Thu Sep 03 2026 
ZCZC MIATCDEP3 ALL
TTAA00 KNHC DDHHMM
 
Hurricane Marie Discussion Number   9
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP132026
200 AM MST Thu Sep 03 2026

Marie continues to gradually become better organized, with very 
deep convection near the center and a more symmetric convective 
pattern.  Satellite estimates have slightly increased since the 
last advisory, and the initial intensity is set to 75 kt, closest 
to the latest TAFB fix.  

The intensity forecast for Marie is tricky.  While it still has a 
couple of days over warm waters with light shear, the structure 
remains somewhat broad, with a large outer wind field.  So far, 
this has prevented anything other than gradual strengthening.  It 
is still a bit curious why most of the guidance don't intensify 
this much during the next day or two, given the conducive 
large-scale environment.  While it is possible that Marie will be 
affected by the wake of Iselle, the forecast track could also be 
far enough away to miss the bulk of the cooler SSTs.  The new 
forecast is raised from the previous one, splitting the difference 
between the higher SHIPS/LGEM/rapid intensification guidance and 
the lower regional hurricane/corrected consensus models.  A steady 
weakening is likely after the system passes over colder waters in 
about 3 days.

Marie is moving west-northwestward at about 9 kt.  There are no 
changes to the previous synoptic pattern as this general course 
is anticipated to continue for the next several days due to a 
narrow ridge to the north.  While this ridge weakens later on, 
Marie should slow down a bit, but stay moving west-northwestward.  
The new forecast is close to an update of the last one, near a 
consensus of the Google DeepMind ensemble mean and the HFIP 
Corrected Consensus HCCA model.

item.title: Hurricane Lowell Public Advisory Number 28
item.description:
Issued at 1100 PM HST Wed Sep 02 2026 
ZCZC HFOTCPCP4 ALL
TTAA00 PHFO DDHHMM
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Lowell Advisory Number  28
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   EP122026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM HST Wed Sep 02 2026
 
...LOWELL FORECAST TO REMAIN A MAJOR HURRICANE FOR THE NEXT SEVERAL 
DAYS...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1100 PM HST...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...13.3N 156.3W
ABOUT 450 MI...725 KM S OF HILO HAWAII
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...145 MPH...230 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 270 DEGREES AT 10 MPH...17 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...941 MB...27.79 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 PM HST (0900 UTC), the center of Hurricane Lowell was
located near latitude 13.3 North, longitude 156.3 West. Lowell is
moving toward the west near 10 mph (17 km/h). This general motion 
with a gradual decrease in forward speed is expected during the next
few days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 145 mph (230 km/h) with higher
gusts.  Lowell is a category 4 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson
Hurricane Wind Scale.  Some fluctuations in intensity are expected
during the next few days. However, Lowell is expected to remain a
major hurricane for the next several days.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 40 miles (65 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 105 miles
(165 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 941 mb (27.79 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Lowell can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header HFOTCDCP4 and WMO header WTPA44 
KPHFO. 

SURF: Swells generated by Lowell are spreading northward and will
affect portions of the Hawaiian Islands during the next several
days. These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and
rip current conditions. Please consult products from your local
weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 500 AM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Blake

item.title: Hurricane Lowell Forecast Discussion Number 27
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM HST Wed Sep 02 2026 
ZCZC HFOTCDCP4 ALL
TTAA00 PHFO DDHHMM
 
Hurricane Lowell Discussion Number  27
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   EP122026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM HST Wed Sep 02 2026


Since the last advisory, Lowell's satellite signature has decayed,
with the cloud tops in the eyewall warming and the eye becoming
less distinct. This has been accompanied by a decrease in satellite
intensity estimates. A NOAA Hurricane Hunter aircraft has reported
700-mb flight-level winds of 135 kt and a minimum central pressure
near 932-933 mb. Based on these data and continuity from the 
previous advisory, the initial intensity is reduced to a possibly 
generous 135 kt. Satellite imagery gives the impression that the 
hurricane is being affected by easterly shear. However, if this is 
the case, the source of the shear is a bit mysterious, as the
available shear diagnostics show shear of less than 10 kt.
 
The initial motion is now 270/9 kt. Currently, Lowell is being
steered by a low- to mid-level ridge to the north, and due to this
the hurricane should continue moving westward for the next 2-3
days. After that, the track of the hurricane will be controlled by
a developing mid- to upper-level trough or low currently seen in
water vapor imagery near 32N 164W. During the next several days,
the global models forecast this feature to move eastward or
southeastward toward the Hawaiian Islands, then turn westward to
the north of Lowell. While this will break down the ridge north of
Lowell and allow it to turn northward, there is a wide spread of
possibilities of when and where this turn will occur. The model
consensus has again shifted a little eastward at day 4-5, and the
new forecast track is again nudged a little eastward at these times.
 
The hurricane is expected to stay in a favorable environment of
high oceanic heat content and low shear for at least the next three
days. However, the intensity guidance calls for slow decay during
this time despite the favorable environment. Based on this, the
intensity forecast also calls for slow decay. It is likely, though,
that eyewall replacement cycles will cause fluctuations in
intensity superimposed on the slow decay.  Near the end of the
forecast period, Lowell should start experiencing increasing shear
caused by the upper-level trough, and a more pronounced weakening
may begin around day 5. There remains high confidence that Lowell
will remain a major hurricane through the weekend.
 
 
KEY MESSAGES:
 
1. The details of Lowell's long-range track and intensity forecasts
are more uncertain than usual, and it is too soon to determine
potential impacts in the Hawaiian Islands.
 
2. Interests in Hawaii should continue to closely monitor the
progress of Lowell through this upcoming weekend. This is a good
time for all residents to ensure they have their hurricane plan and
supply kit in place.
 
3. Swells from Lowell are likely to cause life-threatening surf and
rip current conditions in portions of the Hawaiian Islands during
the next several days.  Depending on the exact track of the storm,
these swells are likely to increase early next week.
